subject: MSA redline: evidence cadence & pen-test alignment
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@brightwell.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redline: evidence cadence & pen-test alignment

Morgan —

Thanks again for the productive conversation yesterday. Attached are two artifacts to kick off the MSA/order form discussion: a first-pass redline focused on the security exhibit (redline-draft.pdf) and an evidence inventory template (evidence-inventory.xlsx).

High-level proposal for alignment so we can move to procurement:
- Evidence cadence: monthly SOC 2-related evidence drops (system configs, controls mapping) + ad-hoc requests tied to incidents.
- Pen-test window: we propose a quarterly 5-business-day staging access window with 30 days' notice; if you need an annual or on-demand full-scope test, we can add that to the order form as an explicit addendum.
- Staging access SLA: Redwood can provide ephemeral staging credentials for up to 5 business days, gating on a 48-hour pre-window ops readiness check.

Questions for you:
1) Does Brightwell have a preferred pen-test vendor or external auditor (we can work directly with them)?
2) Any non-negotiable wording for inspection rights or data sampling we should preserve in the MSA?
3) Target procurement sign-off date — you mentioned late June in our call; is that still accurate?

Next steps we suggest: list agreed-upon windows & sampling bands, Redwood legal and Brightwell legal iterate on a single redline, then we produce an order form insert for DocuSign.

Attachments: redline-draft.pdf (summary redline), evidence-inventory.xlsx (template)

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions PM | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

--

From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@brightwell.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightwell Health Legal <procurement@brightwellhealth.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@svc-audit.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MSA redline: evidence cadence & pen-test alignment

Thanks Rachel — helpful start. A few quick points from our side:

- Vendor preference: we typically use an external pen-test vendor (Alex Turner copied) for full-scope engagements; for smaller, scoped tests we may accept vendor-managed tests but need an audit trail to our vendor.
- Sampling: procurement wants clear language that limits broad production inspection to specific sampled systems/controls. We can accept monthly evidence drops but need a sampling matrix so we don't end up providing full production snapshots monthly.
- Timeline: procurement is still aiming for late June signature, but legal wants to resolve the MSA exhibit language this week.

I've attached Brightwell's standard security questionnaire (brightwell-questionnaire.pdf) — it highlights some of the clauses our legal team will push on (notice period, inspection carve-outs, redaction obligations).

On the pen-test window, the 5-business-day staging access sounds reasonable if we can codify sampling bands and a maximum scope for production-facing systems.

Morgan
Director, IT Security | Brightwell Health
morgan.lee@brightwell.com | +1 617-555-2184

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@brightwell.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline: evidence cadence & pen-test alignment

Morgan / Rachel —

Thanks for the details, Morgan. Quick read-through from legal on the redline attached (legal-redline.docx). Summary of recommended language we believe will keep both sides comfortable:

- Inspection rights: propose explicit sampling bands (e.g., "no more than 10% of production systems per calendar quarter for configuration-level evidence; full system-level access only with mutual written agreement and additional scope addendum").

- Pen-test clause: replace broad "inspection" language with a two-track approach:
  * Scoped staging penetration tests (as Rachel proposed): 5 business days, 30 days' notice, staging credentials ephemeral.
  * Full-scope / production-impact tests: allowed only when backed by a written addendum, minimum 30 days' notice, and constraints on blast radius.

- Evidence retention & redaction: Redwood will provide evidence artifacts with PII redacted; Brightwell may request unredacted samples through a mutually agreed escalation process that includes an NDA and a narrow scope.

Action items for Redwood ops/legal: please incorporate the following changes into the order form insert so procurement can review:
1) Add the sampling band table to the security exhibit (we recommend the attached evidence-inventory template be used as the basis).
2) Add the two-track pen-test addendum language (we provided a short snippet in the attached doc).
3) Provide an estimated ops runbook for staging access (an ETL of steps, plus contact window) — ops can provide a 48-hour readiness checklist.

Ben/Karthik — we need a 24-hour legal turnaround on any changes if Brightwell expects late-June signature. If you can triage the redline today, Rachel will prepare the DocuSign-ready order form.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 650-555-3041

Subject: Re: MSA redline: evidence cadence & pen-test alignment

Quick note from legal — we can accept Laura's recommendations with one adjustment: for sampling bands, replace the hard 10% number with a "reasonably scoped sampling" definition and a concrete escalation path if Brightwell needs broader coverage (to avoid ambiguity in production support).

We also want to preserve Redwood's operational constraint that staging credentials are timeboxed and that any requests that require deeper access trigger our security review (we can include a short form to be completed by the auditor).

Rachel — please:
- Update the redline to reflect the sampling definition tweak (language snippet below).
- Put together the DocuSign-ready order form insert and send to procurement + me.

Language snippet to use: "Customer may request inspection of systems per the sampling bands set forth in the Security Exhibit. Where a request exceeds the agreed sampling bands, the parties will engage the escalation process described in Section X (Escalation & Additional Access), which may include an addendum for expanded scope and mutually agreed mitigation controls."

If Rachel can get the updated doc out by EOD today, we will do the quick legal pass and route to procurement.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-2699
